tools.title: Apartment Application Readiness Checklist
tools.summary: A free apartment application readiness checklist: note what the landlord asked for, gather real proof, and check every date, name, and amount before you apply.
checklist: Photo ID for every adult who will sign the lease.
Pay stubs or a signed offer letter showing the income the form asks for.
Bank statements, if your income is irregular or you are self-employed.
Previous landlords' names and current phone numbers, confirmed before you list them.
Your employer's contact details for the verification call.
The application fee, in the form the leasing office takes.
A written note on anything a screening report will show that you would rather explain yourself.

tools.title: Proof of Income Packet Checklist
tools.summary: A free proof of income packet checklist: pin down the exact request, gather real pay records, and make sure every figure matches before you send it.
checklist: Your two most recent pay stubs, with year-to-date totals visible.
Last year's W-2, or 1099s for any work paid as a contractor.
Last year's federal return with all schedules, if you are self-employed.
Three months of bank statements whose deposits match the income you are stating.
A letter from your employer confirming your role, start date and current pay.
Award letters for income that is not wages: benefits, pension, support.
A one-page summary listing each source of income and its monthly amount.

tools.title: Business Funding Document Checklist
tools.summary: A free business funding document checklist: write down the lender's request, gather true records, and check dates, names, and amounts before you apply.
checklist: Formation documents: articles, your operating agreement, and any DBA filing.
The EIN assignment letter from the IRS.
Business bank statements for the last twelve months.
Business tax returns for the last two years, and personal returns if a guarantee is asked for.
A profit and loss statement and balance sheet, current through last month.
A written note on what the funds are for and how repayment is planned.
Any license, permit or certification your industry requires.

tools.title: Mortgage Document Readiness Checklist
tools.summary: A free mortgage document readiness checklist: capture the underwriter's request, gather real support, and separate what you can prove from context.
checklist: Pay stubs covering your most recent 30 days of income, with year-to-date totals visible.
W-2 forms for the last two years, plus any 1099s for income paid outside payroll.
Federal tax returns for the last two years, with every schedule attached.
Two months of statements for each account holding your down payment or reserves.
A short written note on any deposit that did not come from your employer.
Current statements for the debts underwriting will see: cards, student loans, auto notes.
Photo ID, and your name written exactly as it appears on your tax return.
For any other property you own: the mortgage statement, tax bill and insurance policy.

tools.title: Car Loan Document Checklist
tools.summary: A free car loan document checklist: write down what the lender or dealer asked for, gather real proof, and check every detail before you apply.
checklist: A valid driver's license in the name you will sign the contract under.
Recent pay stubs, or last year's return if you work for yourself.
Proof of insurance, or your agent's details so coverage can start at delivery.
Proof of your current address on a utility bill or bank statement.
The references the lender asks for, with phone numbers you have checked.
If you are trading a vehicle in: its title, registration and current payoff figure.
Your down payment, in a form the dealership will actually accept.

tools.title: Important Documents Folder Checklist
tools.summary: A free checklist for your important documents folder: note who is asking, gather the originals you hold, check each detail, and keep copies of what you send.
checklist: Birth certificates and Social Security cards for everyone in the household.
Passports, and any immigration or naturalization paperwork.
Marriage, divorce or custody documents.
Property deeds, vehicle titles, and the current statement for each loan against them.
Insurance policies: health, auto, home or renters, and life.
Wills, powers of attorney and advance directives, noting where the originals are kept.
Federal tax returns for the last two years.
